title: Introduce graded surge fence and utilization telemetry enhancements
author: Maya Thompson
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets sometimes experience micro-surges that are large enough to cause latency SLO violations for critical tenants but too brief for the existing hard burst-quotas to handle without wasteful long-lived reservations. This PR introduces a graded surge fence: a per-tenant surge controller that enforces short-lived, decaying bandwidth fences with configurable grades (fast/medium/slow) so the autoscaler and gateway can apply differentiated backpressure. The design balances strict throughput guarantees for high-tier tenants with opportunistic capacity sharing for lower tiers.

What this PR does (summary): Adds a GradedSurgeFence controller that tracks instantaneous and short-window token consumption, converts those into a graded reservation token with a decay schedule, and exposes a small admission API for the gateway to consult before accepting bursts. Adds new utilization telemetry (reservoir_pressure, surge_slope, graded_fence_count, per_tenant_headroom) and enriches the capacity export with a short-window decayed-utilization metric. Integrates graded fence signals into the autoscaler decision pipeline so rapid micro-surges will trigger a transient soft-throttle rather than an immediate long-lived scale-up.

Compatibility and rollout: Implementation is opt-in per-pool via a new poolConfig.grading.enabled flag; default is disabled. The rollout plan included a canary in one dedicated fleet, followed by staged enablement across cloud regions. No schema upgrades for persisted objects except a small fence metadata blob which includes grade and expiry timestamp. Migration path: old-runner ignores the flag; new runners read the flag and use default disabled behavior if the field is missing.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for the decay math and admission API. Integration tests exercising gateway backpressure with synthetic microbursts. E2E canary runs on staging showed 18% reduction in sustained scale-ups triggered by microbursts and a 12ms median latency improvement for tier-1 tenants under bursty traffic patterns.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement graded fence controller and API
- [x] Wire telemetry to metrics pipeline and datadog export
- [x] Autoscaler integration for transient soft-throttle
- [x] Gateway admission hook + fallback path
- [x] Unit & integration tests
- [x] Docs: config, rollout, troubleshooting guide

Related: ENG-1842 (graded throttle research spike), ENG-1909 (autoscaler signal plumbing).

Maya Thompson (author): Addressed in commit 4c3b9a6 — switched to sharded ledger with reference to occupancy cache and added benchmarks showing <3% memory uplift on 8k tenants.
Liam Chen: The decay function looks good but please add an explicit unit test covering boundary conditions (expiry exactly at window boundary).
Maya Thompson: Added boundary tests and documented the expected rounding semantics in the comments and docs.
Sofia Martinez: Telemetry names collide with an older metric (pool_pressure). Please rename to reservoir_pressure and update dashboards.

release_notes: Introduce Graded Surge Fence for short-lived micro-surges; new telemetry: reservoir_pressure, surge_slope, graded_fence_count; opt-in per-pool via poolConfig.grading.enabled; autoscaler uses decayed short-window util to avoid unnecessary long-lived scale-ups.
notes_for_ops: Enable poolConfig.grading.enabled on a single canary fleet first. Watch reservoir_pressure and graded_fence_count. If latency regressions occur, disable grading on affected pool. Datadog dashboards updated; alerts added for persistent reservoir_pressure > 0.8 for > 5m.
